overview.workspaceText: Configure your internal workspace and invitation defaults.
overview.knowledgeBaseText: Upload manuals and internal procedures. The assistant cites them in every answer.
overview.chatbotText: Test prompts against the indexed documents from the in-app playground.
overview.sessionText: Upload a document, run a prompt in the chat playground, and inspect the cited sources before sharing the link.

quickstarts.firstUploadText: Add a source file to the workspace knowledge base.
quickstarts.documentsText: Follow pending, processing, completed, and failed states.
quickstarts.playgroundText: Ask a question and review the cited sources.
quickstarts.teamText: Add teammates so the assistant can serve everyone.

overview.employeePath: Works only on documents you uploaded.
overview.adminPath: For administrators who manage members and documents.
overview.ownerPath: Full control over organization SLA timers, template marketplace, and visual app composer.
overview.documentsDescription: Manage uploads, track indexing, and open the knowledge source used by the assistant.
overview.playgroundDescription: Run a prompt against your indexed documents and inspect the cited sources.
overview.citationsText: Every answer links back to the indexed document it used, so reviewers can open the source with one click.
overview.coreFlowAlt: OpenVie knowledge lifecycle: upload documents, index asynchronously, and receive cited answers.
overview.coreFlowCaption: Document lifecycle: ingest source files (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV), vectorize into the workspace knowledge base, and generate citations with every answer.

gettingStarted.signInTitle: Sign in with your company email
gettingStarted.signInText: Use your work email to receive the verification code. Your workspace is determined by your invitation.
gettingStarted.uploadText: Open Documents and upload a file. The system indexes the content automatically.
gettingStarted.uploadBody: Indexing usually completes within a minute. The status changes automatically once processing finishes.
gettingStarted.uploadWarning: Only members of your workspace can see the documents you upload.
gettingStarted.indexText: The status column shows pending, processing, completed, or failed.
gettingStarted.indexBody: Everything indexed becomes available to the assistant with citation links.
gettingStarted.askText: Test a prompt against your document.
gettingStarted.testTip: Check that the answer contains a link to the document you just uploaded.
gettingStarted.testBody: Select a document and ask a question about its content.
gettingStarted.documentsDescription: Manage uploads, track indexing, and open the knowledge source used by the assistant.
gettingStarted.playgroundDescription: Run a prompt against your indexed documents and inspect the cited sources.

documents.pdfDescription: Best for long-form manuals and policies.
documents.textDescription: Plain text notes, README files, and markdown guides.
documents.spreadsheetDescription: Spreadsheets with one row per record.
documents.audioDescription: Audio recordings (.mp3, .wav, .m4a, .flac, .ogg, .opus) transcribed via faster-whisper ASR into time-coded passages.
documents.videoDescription: Video presentations (.mp4, .mov, .mkv, .webm) demuxed into audio for speech recognition and keyframes for OCR.
documents.imageDescription: Diagrams, scans, and screenshots (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp) with Vietnamese/English Tesseract OCR text extraction.
documents.antivirusText: All uploaded files are scanned in real-time. Infected files or test EICAR signatures are automatically rejected (HTTP 422) and quarantined.
documents.limitText: Large files may fail to index. Default limit is 20 MB; split very large files before uploading.
documents.processingText: Text is being extracted and indexed.
documents.completedText: Ready for the assistant to cite.
documents.failedText: Indexing failed. Delete the file and upload it again.
documents.viewerBody: Open a document to preview its extracted content and jump to cited passages.
documents.viewerVerification: Use it to verify that the assistant quotes the passage you expect.
documents.manageBody: Search, filter by status or date, and delete documents you no longer want the assistant to use.
documents.deleteWarning: Deleting a document removes it from every future answer. Earlier chat replies keep their text.

playground.askBody: Type a question in the chat playground. The assistant answers only from your indexed documents.
playground.askTip: Start with a question whose answer you already know to judge the response quality.
playground.sourcesBody: Each answer lists the documents it used, with links back to the source.
playground.sourcesNote: If a source looks wrong, fix the document first, then ask again.
playground.multimodalCitationsText: Clicking timestamp badges ([HH:MM:SS]) automatically seeks the built-in media player to the exact cited second. Clicking image citations opens high-resolution diagrams in a full-screen lightbox zoom modal.
playground.suggestionsText: After grounded answers, clickable suggestion chips propose relevant follow-up questions in the conversation language.
playground.historyBody: Your previous chats are stored in the workspace and can be reopened from the sidebar.
playground.historyRecent: The most recent chat loads automatically when you return to the chat.
playground.historyPrivate: Only members of your workspace can open these chats.
playground.manageBody: Rename or delete chats you no longer need. Deletion is permanent.

workflow.twoLevelBody: Uploaded documents undergo automated sensitivity scoring. Ordinary documents require Level 1 (workspace admin) approval, while sensitive documents or public targets automatically escalate to Level 2 (organization owner) approval.
workflow.sensitivePolicyTip: The shared sensitivity policy evaluates content for confidential and security-critical terms without sending data outside.
workflow.claimBody: Reviewers claim unassigned tasks from the approval inbox (/approvals). After reviewing, choose Approve, Reject (with a mandatory reason), or Escalate.
workflow.slaReminderText: Reminder timer (default 24h): Triggers an automated notification to reviewers when a task remains pending.
workflow.slaEscalationText: Escalation timer (default 48h): Automatically reassigns stalled Level 1 tasks to the Organization Owner to prevent approval bottlenecks.
workflow.memberRoleText: Can submit documents for approval and track progress. Cannot claim approval tasks or modify SLAs.
workflow.adminRoleText: Can claim and decide Level 1 approval tasks, deploy workspace BPMN XML, and manage workspace documents.
workflow.ownerRoleText: Exclusive authority to configure organization SLA timers, approve Level 2 tasks, and manage BizApps.
workflow.approvalInboxDescription: Review pending tasks, inspect documents, and record decisions.
workflow.approvalFlowAlt: Two-level document approval workflow with SLA timers.
workflow.approvalFlowCaption: Multi-stage workflow: documents progress from submitter through Workspace Admin (Level 1) to Organization Owner (Level 2), with automated SLA reminder and escalation timers.

bizapps.introBody: A BizApp is a declarative application that runs directly on OpenVie's headless platform without requiring custom microservices or backends. Everything it does is described by one JSON manifest under the frozen bizapp.v1 contract: entities, executable blocks, declarative reports, role permissions, and runtime views.
bizapps.introStructure: Installing freezes the manifest, deploys the app's approval process (if any), and serves runtime views at /apps/{kind}. The AI assistant can answer questions about app records through knowledge projection with citations.
bizapps.topIdentity: kind is a unique lowercase key per [locale]; name holds vi/en labels and is shown as the app title; version starts at 1 and is bumped automatically on upgrade.
bizapps.topStorage: jsonb is the generic store for custom apps; typed tables are reserved for the platform's bundled templates.
bizapps.topRbac: Capability → workspace role lists. Defaults keep reading open, restrict writes/deletes/approvals to admins, and let submit fall back to write.
bizapps.topEntities: Data models: fields with types string, number, boolean, enum, date, ref; optional knowledge projection and lifecycle hooks.
bizapps.topBlocks: Executable or functional pieces: approval_workitem, notify, webhook_out, external_call, report, knowledge_base, assistant (plus inert registry/form/timeline presentation views).
bizapps.topUi: Runtime view order (registry:/form:/timeline:/report:/assistant:) and canvas layout coordinates.
bizapps.topConversational: Trigger phrases and a short description that help the assistant route messages to this app when the message does not name it.
bizapps.unknownKeysBody: Keys the contract does not declare fail validation with a corrective hint instead of being silently dropped — for example maxLength is corrected to maxLen. This protects AI drafts and hand-edited JSON alike.
bizapps.installBody: Organization Owners manage everything from /admin/apps: the two-layer catalog (platform-bundled CRM, Booking, Signature Request plus your organization's templates), installed apps, drafts, and the credential vault.
bizapps.installInstall: Install accepts a platform:<kind> templateRef, an organization template id, a draft id, or an inline manifest; validation runs again at install time, so a passing draft can still be rejected honestly.
bizapps.installUpgrade: Upgrade keeps the same kind and storage, auto-bumps the version, preserves all records, and rejects upgrades that would remove entities/fields or change types.
bizapps.installUninstall: Uninstall is soft: the app leaves the workspace UI while records and audit history survive.
bizapps.installDrafts: Drafts (AI, canvas, import, remix) never install themselves; every install is an explicit confirmation.
bizapps.templateSourcesBody: Templates travel in openvie.template.v1 envelopes with author, license, source, generator, changes[] and a SHA-256 of the canonical manifest. Import enforces an SPDX license allow-list (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0) and verifies hashes when provided.
bizapps.manifestNotes: Practical rules the validator and payload validator enforce on every write:
bizapps.fieldNames: Field names are lowercase snake_case (maxLen default 1024 for strings, max 2000; the key is maxLen, never maxLength).
bizapps.fieldTypes: enum fields must declare options; ref fields must point at a declared entity; only the email format is validated server-side today.
bizapps.fieldDates: date fields accept ISO dates, d/m/y shorthand, and natural language such as "today", "tomorrow", or Vietnamese weekday names; times normalize to HH:mm.
bizapps.fieldPii: Fields marked pii can never be projected into the knowledge base, regardless of rbac.
bizapps.fieldHooks: Hooks reference hookable block ids (approval_workitem, notify, webhook_out, external_call) or webhook_out:<event>; onDecide is always best-effort and approval blocks may not be targeted by it.
bizapps.viewsIntro: ui.views controls the tabs users see; each view renders from the frozen manifest:
bizapps.viewRegistry: Registry View: paged table (updated_at desc), create/edit/archive, submit for approval when the app has an approval block, and CSV/Excel export of every active record (10,000-row cap).
bizapps.viewForm: Form View: same table with the create dialog pre-opened; forms are generated from the manifest so undeclared fields cannot even be typed.
bizapps.viewTimeline: Timeline View: card feed of the newest records with the first fields and a status badge.
bizapps.viewReport: Report View: a workspace-admin table for one declarative view; the screen shows the first six columns while export returns every column and row.
bizapps.viewAssistant: Assistant View: an in-app chat panel that reuses the workspace chat session and shows the block's instructions.
bizapps.recordStatus: Records are soft-archived (no hard delete). Archived records stay out of list/report/export unless explicitly included.
bizapps.recordApproval: Submit starts the Flowable process; editing a PENDING record keeps its process alive, and a final decision writes approvalStatus plus processId back into runtime.
bizapps.recordFenceBody: Roles are re-derived per request from the session and organization; client roles are never trusted. Entities and payload fields outside the manifest answer 404/400 respectively. Report execution is workspace-admin only, independent of manifest rbac.
bizapps.reportsIntro: Reports are declarative views inside a report block — no SQL strings anywhere:
bizapps.reportsSpec: name/entity plus optional title, fields (list views), groupBy + metrics (count/sum/avg/min/max with unique aliases), filters (eq ne in gt gte lt lte contains isnull with runtime params), orderBy (must target declared fields or aliases), and limit 1..500 (default 100).
bizapps.reportsAdmin: The compiler always injects org/tenant/app/entity/status='ACTIVE' and binds every value as a named parameter; the source table is fixed by the storage layer.
bizapps.reportsExport: Registry export writes every active record; report export writes every column/row of the view. CSV is UTF-8 with a BOM, fully quoted, spreadsheet-formula safe; Excel keeps numbers numeric.
bizapps.knowledgeBody: Entities with knowledge.project mirror each record into a Markdown knowledge document (declared non-PII fields only) and produce bizapp__<kind>__digest.md, which renders every declared report view as a Markdown table with a 30-second debounce.
bizapps.knowledgeTarget: Chat retrieves only the session chatbot's knowledge base. Point the installation's config.knowledgeBaseId at the workspace default (PATCH /bizapps/{kind}/config) and touch a record so projection lands where chat can read it.
bizapps.knowledgeDebounce: Digest rebuilds are debounced per (workspace, app); install/uninstall never writes documents, so streaming chats never hit revision conflicts from app lifecycle changes.
bizapps.coverageTitle: Coverage is not guaranteed by retrieval
bizapps.coverageBody: Chat answers are top-K retrieval — not a scan over all records. Treat report views (and their exports) as the authority for exact aggregates; the digest helps but depends on declared views staying fresh.
bizapps.vaultBody: The credential vault (owner-only, /admin/apps) stores outbound secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted. Plaintext exists exactly once, only in the create request; listings, reads and exports show metadata only.
bizapps.vaultApiKey: Sent as X-API-Key on connector calls.
bizapps.vaultBasic: Sent as Authorization: Basic base64(user:secret); user is required.
bizapps.vaultOauth2: client-credentials token endpoint via auth.oauth2 (https tokenUrl + credentialRef), token cache refreshed at ~80% TTL.
bizapps.vaultMqtt: Connects MQTT brokers with username/password; user is required.
bizapps.vaultHmac: Signing secret stored as an hmac vault entry; requests sign the timestamp and body headers (X-OpenVie-Signature / X-OpenVie-Timestamp by default).
bizapps.vaultScoping: Credentials are organization-wide by default or scoped to one workspace by id; manifests reference them by name (credentialRef) and resolution prefers the workspace-scoped entry.
bizapps.vaultPem: PEM private keys are rejected outright — OpenVie never holds signing keys; e-signature flows delegate to external providers.
bizapps.vaultEncKey: Key storage requires BIZAPP_ENC_KEY (32 random bytes, base64); without it the vault answers 500 instead of writing plaintext.
bizapps.appsDescription: Every active app opens at /apps/{kind} with the runtime views defined by its manifest.
bizapps.composerLinkDescription: Build or edit app manifests on the canvas, run report builder, and draft with AI.

composer.canvasBody: Build and customize business apps at /admin/apps/compose (new or from a template) and /admin/apps/compose/{draftId}. Work on a React Flow canvas, in an accessible list of entities and blocks, or directly in the canonical bizapp.v1 JSON.
composer.canvasTabs: Three header tabs — Canvas, List, JSON — stay in sync: any edit on one surface regenerates the others and re-runs validation (debounced 400ms against POST /bizapps/validate). Install stays disabled while validation is red.
composer.canvasEdges: Drag entity → block to create a hook edge; click an edge to switch onCreate/onUpdate/onDecide or delete it. Duplicating a pair is prevented, and hooks are the only edges that change the manifest.
composer.canvasDerived: Derived edges are readable views of the manifest: ref fields (entity→entity), report views (block→entity — removing a view from the dialog deletes the real view), connector schedules (dashed, read-only), and assistant→knowledge-base links.
composer.canvasValidation: The bottom validation panel lists every validation error translated into plain language; the rename dialog keeps vi/en titles valid for the manifest.
composer.autoLayoutTip: Use the Auto Layout button to automatically organize complex entity and block dependency graphs using Dagre.
composer.entityNodeText: Entity inspector: name, EN label, and the field list (types string/number/boolean/enum/date/ref, required, PII). Deep field settings — vi/en labels, maxLen, format, options, optionLabels, knowledge — go through the JSON tab.
composer.entityDeep: The palette adds entities and blocks with safe defaults: a report block starts with one view for the first entity, a webhook declares record.created/record.updated, notify defaults to creator, approval uses the single-process preset with WORKSPACE_ADMIN.
composer.blockNodeText: Block inspectors expose only what matters per type; everything else appears under Additional settings as typed editors (boolean checkbox, number input, string/object lists).
composer.blockDefaults: Blocks only take effect when a hook reaches them; the approval block may also stay standalone so users can submit records manually.
composer.blockApproval: Approver role plus single/two-level presets (choice of bundled BPMN); missing custom templates fall back to the generic single-approval process at install. SLA reminder/escalation durations are configurable per manifest.
composer.blockNotify: Recipients (creator, record.<email field>, config.<key>, or a literal address) plus title/subject templates with {{record.field}} placeholders. Delivery failures are audited, never rolled back.
composer.blockWebhook: Checkbox list of standard record events; custom events come from hook targets webhook_out:<event>. Events fan out after commit.
composer.blockExternal: HTTP/MQTT connector: url (or brokerUrl+topic), credentialRef, method (GET/HEAD send no body), bodyTemplate, responseMap JSON pointers, field/record sinks with dedupeKey, schedule PT30S..P7D, timeouts and retries.
composer.blockKnowledge: The app's knowledge base is created automatically; graphExtraction is optional. Nothing to configure.
composer.blockAssistant: Instructions shown on the assistant tab; the panel reuses the workspace chat session.
composer.reportBuilderBody: The report builder edits a declarative view without SQL: title (which generates a slug name), entity, and a list/summary mode.
composer.reportModes: List mode picks columns from declared fields; summary mode composes groupBy columns plus metric values.
composer.reportMetrics: Metrics are count/sum/avg/min/max with unique aliases; sum/avg require a number field. Changing the entity resets grouping and metrics.
composer.reportFilters: Filters use operators eq ne in gt gte lt lte isnull with literal values (or runtime params in the JSON tab), and sorting targets fields or aliases, then limit is bounded to 500.
composer.reportLimit: Every view keeps limit 1..500 (default 100); the SQL always applies it, so exports stay bounded.
composer.reportRuntimeBody: The report tab is workspace-admin only; the table shows the first six columns while export returns all columns and rows. Engine stays postgres unless the JSON declares lakehouse.
composer.aiDraftingBody: Describe the desired business process in plain language (e.g., 'Asset tracking app for IT hardware'). The generator produces a manifest draft that is validated twice — first against the frozen bizapp.v1 schema during structured generation, then again by the same validator used by the composer.
composer.aiDraftingFlow: Generation runs up to three validation-repair attempts with the primary model, then falls back to the configured secondary model once. Drafts carry model/attempts metadata and never install themselves; /admin/apps also offers drafting from the last 20 turns of a chat session (from-chat), still draft-only.
composer.aiDraftingTip: Drafts never install automatically. Review, edit and re-validate on the canvas; only an explicit install button deploys anything.
composer.templateExchangeBody: Templates travel in openvie.template.v1 envelopes: meta (author, license, source, generator, changes[]) plus the canonical manifest and its SHA-256.
composer.templateExport: Export downloads the envelope for any templateRef (platform:<kind> or an organization template id); envelopes that do not exist yet are built on the fly.
composer.templateImport: Import accepts pasted envelope JSON or a catalog URL. URL import is restricted to hosts in BIZAPPS_REMOTE_CATALOG_HOSTS and can verify the expected SHA-256; an invalid hash or a checksum mismatch rejects the import.
composer.templateLicenses: Import enforces the SPDX license allow-list (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, CC0-1.0, CC-BY-4.0) and re-validates the manifest; the result is always a draft, never an install.
composer.templateRemix: Remix forks a template into a new draft while keeping upstream author/license/source and appending a dated change entry.
composer.upgradeBody: Install is idempotent about upgrades: a draft whose kind is already active upgrades in place instead of answering 'already installed'.
composer.upgradeVersion: Upgrade auto-bumps the version to max(current + 1, requested), records it in the stored manifest, and redeploys the approval process when the approver role changes (pending tasks are reassigned).
composer.upgradeCompatible: Upgrades preserve records: same storage engine, no removed entity/field, no changed field type. Delete is rejected up-front so no data is lost.
composer.draftsBody: Drafts (AI, canvas, import, remix) are owned by the organization, can be opened in the composer, and are deleted explicitly. Publishing a template is currently API-only (POST /marketplace/bizapps).
composer.openComposerDescription: Open the visual drag-and-drop editor to create or modify BizApp manifests.

auth.passwordSsoBody: OpenVie supports direct password-based sign-in as well as enterprise Single Sign-On (SSO) via OpenID Connect (Keycloak). Organization members can log in using either their company email and password or by clicking the SSO provider button.
auth.ssoTip: When SSO is configured, users authenticate against your enterprise directory without needing a separate OpenVie password.
auth.firstLoginBody: When an administrator provisions your account, you will receive an initial temporary password or an invitation link. Upon your first sign-in, OpenVie requires you to change your temporary password before accessing workspaces.
auth.passwordRequirement: New passwords must be at least 8 characters long and contain a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters.
auth.securityTip: Never transmit temporary or permanent credentials over unsecured chat or email channels.
auth.switchWorkspaceBody: OpenVie provides isolated workspaces for different departments and projects. You can switch between authorized workspaces from the workspace switcher in the top navigation bar at any time.
auth.languageBody: To switch between Vietnamese and English, use the locale selector in the navigation bar. Your selection persists across sessions.
auth.workspaceDataNote: All uploaded documents, conversations, and search indexes are strictly isolated to the active workspace.
auth.recoverAccessBody: If you forget your password or lose access to your account, reach out to your Organization Owner or Administrator. Administrators can reset passwords or generate new invitation links from the organization admin console.
auth.ssoRecoveryNote: For SSO accounts, password resets must be performed through your corporate identity provider (IdP).
auth.memberDocDesc: Learn how administrators provision accounts and assign workspace roles.
auth.loginDesc: Return to the login screen to sign in or accept an invitation.

members.orgAccountsBody: OpenVie organizes user access into two tiers: Organization Accounts and Workspace Memberships. An organization account establishes a user identity across the company, while workspace memberships grant access to specific document sets and approval queues.
members.roleOwnerText: Full administrative control over all workspaces, billing, organization settings, and API keys.
members.roleAdminText: Can create accounts, manage workspace allocations, and inspect audit logs.
members.roleMemberText: Accesses only the specific workspaces they have been invited into.
members.createAccountBody: Organization Owners and Admins create new user accounts from the Organization Admin console (/admin/organization).
members.createStep1: Open the Organization Admin page (/admin/organization) and click the 'Create user' button.
members.createStep2: Provide the user's corporate email, full name, and assign an organization role.
members.createStep3: Set an initial temporary password or choose to send an activation invitation.
members.inviteWorkspaceBody: After creating an account, assign the user to one or more workspaces from the Workspaces console (/admin/workspaces) or the workspace member management tab.
members.inviteStep1: Select the target workspace from the workspace list.
members.inviteStep2: Click 'Add member' and search for the user by name or email.
members.inviteStep3: Select the workspace role (WORKSPACE_ADMIN or MEMBER) and confirm.
members.passwordStatusBody: Administrators can reset user passwords, activate, deactivate, or permanently remove accounts at any time from the organization console.
members.deactivateWarning: Deactivating an account immediately blocks sign-in while preserving the user's historical document uploads and approval logs.
members.adminOrgDesc: Manage user accounts, invitations, and permissions.
members.workspacesDesc: Assign members and configure workspace access.

workspaces.defaultWorkspaceBody: Every OpenVie organization includes a default workspace (General). The default workspace serves as the common repository for company-wide documentation, standard operating procedures, and shared guidelines.
workspaces.defaultWorkspaceNote: All new organization members are granted access to the default workspace by default, ensuring immediate access to foundational resources.
workspaces.visibilityBody: Workspaces can be configured as either Public or Private depending on the confidentiality of the materials they contain.
workspaces.publicVisibilityText: Discoverable and accessible by all members of the organization. Ideal for cross-departmental documentation, company policies, and training materials.
workspaces.privateVisibilityText: Restricted exclusively to explicitly invited members. Critical for human resources, legal affairs, financial audits, and executive strategy.
workspaces.lifecycleBody: Workspaces follow a structured lifecycle: creation, active operation, archiving, and deletion.
workspaces.lifecycleCreate: Create: Define name, description, and visibility when establishing a new department or project.
workspaces.lifecycleArchive: Archive: Sets the workspace to read-only mode. Members can still query existing documents and chat history, but new uploads and edits are blocked.
workspaces.lifecycleDelete: Delete: Permanently purges all documents, vector embeddings, and conversation histories associated with the workspace. Only Organization Owners can delete workspaces.
workspaces.archiveWarning: Deleting a workspace cannot be undone. Always archive first if there is any requirement for regulatory record retention.
workspaces.membershipBody: Workspace members interact with knowledge bases and approval queues based on their assigned workspace role.
workspaces.roleAdminNote: WORKSPACE_ADMIN can upload documents, trigger re-indexing, review Level 1 approvals, and manage membership.
workspaces.roleMemberNote: MEMBER can ask questions in the chat playground, view citations, and submit documents for review.
workspaces.documentsDesc: Learn how documents are indexed and isolated per workspace.
workspaces.workspacesAdminDesc: Create, configure, and monitor your workspaces.

settings.orgProfileBody: The Organization Profile defines your organization's legal identity, display name, slug, and contact email within OpenVie.
settings.orgProfileTip: Keep your organization contact email up to date to ensure critical administrative alerts and security notifications are delivered.
settings.selfRegBody: The self-registration toggle controls whether new users can independently sign up via the public /register page.
settings.selfRegEnabled: When enabled, visitors with corporate email addresses can create accounts without prior administrative invitation.
settings.selfRegDisabled: When disabled, registration is invitation-only. All accounts must be explicitly created by Organization Admins.
settings.selfRegSecurity: For enterprise deployments, we recommend keeping self-registration disabled and managing provisioning through SSO or administrative invites.
settings.emailChannelsBody: OpenVie uses SMTP email channels to deliver invitation emails, password reset links, and workflow SLA reminder notifications.
settings.smtpFieldHost: SMTP Host and Port (e.g., smtp.sendgrid.net:587 or email-smtp.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:465).
settings.smtpFieldAuth: Username, password or API token, and TLS/STARTTLS security protocol.
settings.smtpFieldFrom: Sender email address and display name shown to recipients.
settings.testEmailTip: Use the 'Send test email' button in the settings console to verify your SMTP credentials and delivery connectivity immediately.
settings.authDesc: Review login options, password policies, and SSO integration.
settings.settingsConsoleDesc: Configure profile, email channels, and registration policies.

apiKeys.whenBody: OpenVie provides a headless architecture, allowing internal enterprise applications, custom chatbots, CRM bridges, and workflow bots to interact with your knowledge base directly over REST APIs without using the web interface.
apiKeys.whenTip: Use API keys for machine-to-machine integrations. For interactive human users, always authenticate using standard web sessions or SSO.
apiKeys.createBody: Organization Owners can create API keys from the Organization Admin console (/admin/organization/api-keys). Each key is bound to a single workspace and assigned a specific role (WORKSPACE_ADMIN or MEMBER).
apiKeys.createFigureAlt: API key creation dialog in the organization admin console.
apiKeys.createFigureCaption: API key creation dialog: set a descriptive name, select the bound workspace, assign the service role, and optionally specify an expiration date.
apiKeys.paramName: Descriptive name for the integration (e.g., 'Internal CRM Bridge'). Maximum 120 characters.
apiKeys.paramWorkspace: Target workspace identifier whose documents and chat sessions this key can access.
apiKeys.paramRole: Permission level within the bound workspace: WORKSPACE_ADMIN or MEMBER.
apiKeys.paramExpiry: Optional ISO 8601 expiration date. Requests made after this time return 401 Unauthorized.
apiKeys.secretOnceBody: When an API key is created, OpenVie generates a cryptographically secure token prefixed with ovk_. This full secret is displayed exactly once in a modal dialog. OpenVie stores only a SHA-256 hash of the secret in the database.
apiKeys.secretFigureAlt: One-time API key secret display modal with copy button and warning.
apiKeys.secretFigureCaption: One-time secret display: copy the ovk_ secret immediately and save it in a secure password vault before clicking acknowledge.
apiKeys.secretSecurity: Never expose your API key secret in client-side code, frontend bundles, or public version control. If a secret is lost or compromised, revoke it immediately.
apiKeys.manageBody: The API Keys console lists all active and revoked keys. You can monitor key usage, check expiration dates, and revoke compromised keys with immediate effect.
apiKeys.tableFigureAlt: API keys administration table displaying active and revoked keys.
apiKeys.tableFigureCaption: API keys table: review key names, bound workspaces, service roles, real-time statuses, and revoke access with a single click.
apiKeys.revokeWarning: Revoking a key is permanent and instantaneous. Any automated services currently using the key will immediately receive 401 Unauthorized.
apiKeys.firstCallsBody: Once you have your API key, you can start integrating OpenVie into your systems using standard HTTP requests.
apiKeys.call3Title: 3. Send a chat query with cited response
apiKeys.apiKeysConsoleDesc: Generate and manage machine API keys for your organization.
apiKeys.playgroundDesc: Test queries interactively before integrating into your applications.

ApiKeys.title: API keys
ApiKeys.description: Machine-to-machine keys authenticate as a service member inside the workspace bound to the key. The secret (ovk_…) is shown exactly once right after creation.
ApiKeys.createDescription: The key is permanently bound to one workspace and operates with the chosen role — it cannot be moved later.
ApiKeys.name: Key name
ApiKeys.workspaceHint: The key only works inside this workspace: sessions, knowledge base, and permissions all derive from it — pick where the integrating app will operate.
ApiKeys.roleHint: MEMBER is enough for chat and document reads; WORKSPACE_ADMIN only if the app manages members.
ApiKeys.expiryHint: Leave empty for a key that never expires; an expired key answers 401.
ApiKeys.createdDescription: The only copy of the secret — copy it now.
ApiKeys.createdWarning: This is the only time the secret is shown. Never paste it into frontend code; keep it in a server-side secret manager.
ApiKeys.copyFailed: Copy failed; select the text and copy manually.
ApiKeys.revokeDescription: The key stops authenticating immediately and its service account is suspended. Applications still using it will receive 401.
ApiKeys.validWorkspace: Choose a workspace for the key.
ApiKeys.validExpiryFuture: Expiry must be in the future.
